searchText: I can add this as part of the London spec if that’s helpful 👍 Happy to take a first stab at it and tag client teams to review PRs to make sure it’s accurate. thanks! when would you say this was last modified? like, Homestead? It says 2019 but I think the modifications were tiny since around 2016 resource pricing has always been unclear to me, maybe because it's not really an ongoing area of consistent research, so there aren't "up-to-date" resources for it any idea where to find anything on the new methodolody? There are various scattered writings So I think it depends which subproblem you are interested in There are basically two sub-problems gotcha 1. How to price computing vs bandwidth vs storage 2. How to determine the computation time of various opcodes/precompiles, so we can give all the different types of computing the same ratio of price-to-effort (1) is more of a "deep thinking" problem, (2) is more of an empirical/coding/benchmarking problem The alternative to 3403 is here: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3529 Join the EIP-3074: AUTH and AUTHCALL opcodes community call for Q&A with co-authors, today at 1600UTC (~in 4 hrs). https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/303 Why `NEW_MAX_REFUND_QUOTIENT` not `MAX_REFUND_QUOTIENT`? Because the current `MAX_REFUND_QUOTIENT` is 2 (it's not documented as a constant but it arguably is) But I'm happy with just calling it `MAX_REFUND_QUOTIENT` too (starting in 10 mins) Join Zoom Meeting https://us02web.zoom.us/j/83343120771?pwd=bW0wckdnUFdFTzE4SHZ2U0xvSXQ3dz09 Meeting ID: 833 4312 0771 Passcode: 427068 I believe in many other EIPs is rather "change the constant `MAX_REFUND_QUOTIENT` from 2 to 5". I prefer doing it this way (in this case you would need also to introduce the constant name). But not a blocker to me. I'm happy with any rewording; if someone wants to go edit it to something better I don't oppose Hey folks, looking for feedback and help on this network crawler I built with Apache Tuweni. excerpts.content:
resource pricing has always been unclear to me, maybe because it's not really an ongoing area of consistent research, so there aren't "up-to-date" resources for it

any idea where to find anything on the new methodolody?

excerpts.content: There are various scattered writings

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: So I think it depends which subproblem you are interested in

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: There are basically two sub-problems

excerpts.author: trent_vanepps
excerpts.content: gotcha

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content:
1. How to price computing vs bandwidth vs storage
2. How to determine the computation time of various opcodes/precompiles, so we can give all the different types of computing the same ratio of price-to-effort

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: (1) is more of a "deep thinking" problem, (2) is more of an empirical/coding/benchmarking problem
